references.text: The description of the curtain (parokhet) that separated the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place, the same curtain mentioned in 27:21.
The testimony (ha'edut), referring to the ark of the testimony where the tablets of the law were kept.
Aaron was to trim the lamps morning and evening, the same service described in 27:21.
Reiteration of the command to keep the lamps burning continually before the LORD.
Aaron lights the lamps on the lampstand as he was commanded.
God's lamp continued to burn in the temple of the LORD, showing that this eternal statute was observed.
The Levites kept the lamps burning each evening as part of the temple service.
Another eternal statute (chukat olam) given to Aaron and his sons.
The priesthood given to Aaron and his sons as an eternal statute.
Description of the furnishings of the tabernacle, including the lampstand, and the daily service of the priests.
A direct parallel confirming the eternal arrangement for tending the lamps in the tent of meeting.
Thematic parallel: The two continual offerings (light and bread) that are to stand before the LORD.
Complementary action: The incense offering takes place exactly when the lamps are lit, as part of the same evening ritual.
